title: Knowledge Check 9 - Lessons 41-45
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 41-45 - AI Agents | Testing, Deployment, and Maintenance. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: A support manager asks for an agent that lets signed-in customers on a portal view their own past cases and open a new one. Which type and mechanism fit?
options: A Service agent on an enhanced messaging channel with credential-based verification, so the signed-in customer runs as their own site user and sees only their cases
An Employee agent assigned to each customer
A Lead Nurturing agent
A retired Agentforce (Default) agent
questions.explanation: The audience is external customers, so it is a Service agent, and credential-based verification is what limits each customer to their own records rather than the agent user's broader access.

questions.question: A firm wants the agent to email cold prospects and nurture them toward a meeting. Which choice fits?
options: An Employee agent in Slack
A Service agent on Enhanced Chat
A Lead Nurturing agent, because the job is automated outbound email to prospects
A prompt template with no agent
questions.explanation: Automated outbound prospect email is the Lead Nurturing template's job, which separates it from both an Employee agent and an inbound Service agent.

questions.question: An operations team wants an agent in Slack that answers reps' questions about pipeline and drafts account summaries. Which type fits?
options: A Service agent on Enhanced Chat
An Employee agent, because the users are authenticated internal staff on an internal channel
A Lead Nurturing agent
A public Service agent on the website
questions.explanation: The audience is authenticated internal staff on an internal channel, so the agent runs as the logged-in rep, which is an Employee agent regardless of the chat surface.

questions.question: An integration team asks for the base URL to call against when starting an Agentforce agent session. What is the correct answer?
options: The org's instance URL from My Domain
The Experience Cloud site URL
The login URL of the org
A fixed api.salesforce.com host, with the agent endpoints under the /einstein/ai-agent/v1 path, and the instance endpoint passed inside the session payload
questions.explanation: Agent API is served from the fixed api.salesforce.com base, and the org's instance endpoint is supplied in the start session payload rather than used as the API base.

questions.question: An external service authenticates with the client credentials flow and has no interactive user. Which session setting makes the agent run correctly?
options: Set bypassUser to true so the session uses the agent's own user
Set bypassUser to false and rely on the shared token user
Leave bypassUser out and let it default
Disable the session entirely
questions.explanation: The client credentials flow has no interactive user, so the session should run as the agent user, which is what bypassUser set to true selects.

questions.question: A developer plans to pass an account id into the conversation after the session has already started, as context for the agent's reasoning. What should the consultant advise?
options: Set the context variables the reasoning needs in the start session call, because context variables are read-only after the session begins
Add them to the first message, since context sets at any time
Store them in a Flow variable
Change the instance endpoint mid session
questions.explanation: Most context variables are read-only once the session starts, so the starting context belongs in the start session payload rather than the first message.

questions.question: An external service wants to call the agent and immediately use a structured value the agent's action produced, without dealing with a chat UI. Which shape fits?
options: An Employee agent in Slack
Agent API in a single-turn synchronous call, reading the structured output variables from the response
A prompt template in Prompt Builder
A public Service agent with no integration
questions.explanation: The caller wants a programmatic request-response with structured output, which is exactly the synchronous Agent API pattern, not a chat surface.

questions.question: A chat widget holds a multi turn conversation with a customer and the agent must remember earlier questions. What should the integration do?
options: Create a new session for every message
Pass every earlier message again in each call
Create the session once and reuse the session id across turns so the agent retains context
Disable sessions entirely
questions.explanation: Multi-turn continuity comes from creating the session once and reusing its id, so the agent keeps the conversational context without the caller re supplying it.

questions.question: An integration must carry a specific customer's identity through to Salesforce so their own access governs the agent. Which approach fits?
options: Expose the client credential token in the browser
A shared integration user for everyone
A wrapper that strips identity for speed
An OAuth 2.0 token exchange flow that presents the user's identity provider token and maps it to a Salesforce user
questions.explanation: Token exchange carries the person's identity across the hop and maps it to a Salesforce user, instead of collapsing every caller into one shared service account.

questions.question: A built-in Flow on a case record must have the agent summarize the case and write a field when a rep clicks a button. Which seam fits?
options: An AI Agent action invoked from Flow, because the caller is inside Salesforce and runs under the running user
Agent API with a client credential token
A custom mobile app
An external wrapper with polling
questions.explanation: When the caller is already inside Salesforce, a Flow callout invokes the agent under the running user with no external token, base URL, or session to manage.

questions.question: A customer's own mobile app must embed the agent and pass its signed-in user's identity so that user's access governs. Which approach fits?
options: A retired default agent
A Salesforce Flow scheduled job
Agent API with an identity carrying OAuth flow such as token exchange, so the user's identity crosses the boundary
A prompt template with no agent
questions.explanation: An external customer built surface that must propagate a specific user's identity calls for Agent API with a flow that carries that identity rather than a shared service account.

questions.question: A back office service with no user interface must call the agent nightly to triage cases. Which choice fits?
options: A native chat channel
Agent API using the client credentials flow, running as a dedicated integration user
An Employee agent in Slack
A public Service agent on the website
questions.explanation: A headless service invocation with no human is the client credentials pattern on Agent API, running as its own integration identity.

questions.question: A team wants to iterate quickly on conversation logic without touching the live org or consuming external service calls. Which data access mode do they use?
options: Live Data, because it reflects production behavior
Mocked Data, which runs in an isolated environment that does not connect to external services or affect the active org
Either mode, because the mode only changes reporting
Mocked Data, because it also supports conversation-level testing
questions.explanation: Mocked Data isolates the run from external services and from the active org, which is what fast iteration needs, while conversation-level testing requires live data.

questions.question: You generated multi-turn test cases from your subagents and want each case to open with prior turns the agent must carry. What must you do?
options: Regenerate the set with history enabled, because generated cases already include the prior turns
Add the turns as context variables on the case
Switch the suite to Mocked Data so history is applied
Add the preceding utterances to the conversation history column yourself, because conversation history is a column in the downloadable CSV template and is not factored into generated test cases
questions.explanation: Conversation history is a CSV template column that generated cases do not include, so a multi-turn scenario needs those turns written in by hand.

questions.question: Which statement matches how Testing Center sits alongside the testing you do in Agentforce Builder?
options: Builder preview and Live Test debug a single conversation, while Testing Center runs a suite of cases to score breadth before a release
Testing Center replaces Live Test, which is retired
Builder Live Test requires a CSV upload before it will run
Testing Center runs only from the legacy Setup page
questions.explanation: Builder tests one conversation in real time, including actions against real records, while Testing Center runs many cases to measure routing, actions, and response quality at scale.
